items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Stanley Kay, the drummer with Shorty Sherock’s orchestra... Stanley Kay is the founding father of that band, and he manages them

ctx.x: The Juggernaut band, in fact we talked to Frank Capp in Los Angeles.

Oh did you? Well Nat I think this was his first professional job. Stanley Kay, the drummer with Shorty Sherock’s orchestra was in a record store in Boston buying some Basie records. And before he got, they had little booths in those days. You went in a little glass-enclosed booth and there were individual machines, you could play records. So as he hadn’t even put his records on the turntable, and he heard the very ones that he was buying from the next booth. He thought, I’ve got to meet this guy. And he went in…
Do you still see the Basie band in their present form?

items.title: Stanley Kay interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001
items.q: And we honored Nancy Wilson. © Fillius Jazz Archive -19- And Jean Bach and Virginia Whips, our publicist, and Viola Smith, the drummer who played with Phil Spitalny. But we honored Nancy Wilson.

ctx.x: Yeah. I congratulate you on the work that you’re doing with the band.

Well I congratulate my band, our band. Sometimes I say my — it’s not mine it’s our band, it’s Sherrie’s and my band. I congratulate them because without the product I could maneuver all day long, but without the product I would have nothing. We’ve got a good product. We’ve got a great product. And I’m just hoping that people realize it, and give us a chance. You know the thing is that I went to the former president and vice president of Lippit, Harvey Schiller, through the Yankees. This is Yankee Nets now they…

And Jean Bach and Virginia Whips, our publicist, and Viola Smith, the drummer who played with Phil Spitalny. But we honored Nancy Wilson. And she gave us a great compliment. And I talked to John Levy, because you mentioned about John, and she said I’ve worked for 50 years and I’ve played with a lot of orchestras and this is one of the finest I ever worked with. So she wants to go on tour with us. And we got our first date in September of this year in Tanglewood. And I talked to John about it you see. And she said…
